_README: Regression set for retrieval and answer quality. Run after any change to
search-term generation, tier filters, the quality floor, scoring, or the
library/live routing gate.
Every number the project currently quotes about its own behaviour is a
single live observation. This file exists so those become tracked metrics.
Run with: python eval/run_eval.py
Fields per case:
id                 stable slug
question           exactly as a clinician would type it
mode               review | learn
force_route        live | library — PIN the retrieval path for this case
expect.route       the route the run must actually take
expect.min_papers  floor on evidence-base size
expect.min_sr      minimum Cochrane + Level I papers
expect.min_rct     minimum Level I papers
expect.min_hits_per_query  live only: mean PMIDs esearch returned
per query, read from pubmed_audit.jsonl. Per-query,
not total - the term generator varies its term count
expect.max_empty_fraction  live only: max share of queries returning zero
expect.cochrane_papers_must_be_cochrane_journal  every cochrane-tier
paper's journal must be the Cochrane Database
expect.modules_non_empty   learn mode: every module must be generated
expect.max_unsourced_numeric_modules  modules with numeric params and 0 citations
why                what this case is guarding against
ALWAYS SET force_route. A case without it measures whichever path the
library happens to favour that day, and write-back moves that line under
you: the laser case was written for a live search-term bug, then the fixed
run wrote 196 papers into the library and the same case silently began
testing the library path instead. A topic worth testing on both paths gets
two cases, one pinned each way.
TO FILL IN: cases 3-20. Half should be topics the library covers well and
half genuinely thin. That split is a clinical judgement call — it needs RB,
not the model, or the baseline measures assumptions rather than reality.

cases.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
why: Retrieval regression, 2026-08-29. esearch returned 5 PMIDs across 28
queries because module search strings were bags of words that PubMed
ANDs together ('laser irradiation power settings endodontic
disinfection' matches 1 record in all of PubMed). Module 4 retrieved
zero papers and still emitted a numeric protocol - Er:YAG 20 mJ/15 Hz,
5.25% NaOCl 2 mL/60 s, ISO #30/.04 - invented and shipped behind a
disclaimer.
This topic is also a vocabulary trap: the literature lives under aPDT,
PIPS, SWEEPS, photodynamic therapy and Er:YAG, so any query that does
not OR-expand synonyms will miss it while appearing to succeed.
The first post-fix run reported 10 Cochrane reviews, which is not a
plausible number for this topic and was not real. COCHRANE_TERM was
'Cochrane Review[pt]', a publication type PubMed does not have; it was
translated to a word match on 'cochrane' ANDed with Review[pt], so any
SR that mentioned searching the Cochrane Library was promoted to the
top tier. Fixed to a journal-scoped filter. 109 library rows carrying
the false tag were demoted and rescored (median -7.8).
This case is PINNED to the live route. The bug was in live search-term
generation. The first fixed run wrote 196 papers back into the library,
so without the pin this question would serve from the library and the
term generator - the thing that actually broke - would never run. The
next '3-7 words' regression would pass the eval silently.
min_hits_per_query and max_empty_queries guard the real failure signal,
read from pubmed_audit.jsonl rather than from the evidence dict. The
visible symptom was a small evidence base, but the cause was esearch
itself returning almost nothing, and by the time papers reach the
evidence dict they have already passed the per-tier quality threshold -
a count taken there just shadows the paper count and says nothing about
whether the QUERY was broken. Measured from the audit log:
failing run  28 queries     5 hits   25 empty    0.2 hits/query
fixed run    28 queries   940 hits    0 empty   33.6 hits/query
eval run A   56 queries  2305 hits    7 empty   41.2 hits/query
eval run B    7 queries   205 hits    0 empty   29.3 hits/query
PER QUERY, not total. The term generator's output count varied with
parse luck - measured 5/10 Haiku responses were unparseable because
the model emits PubMed phrase quotes unescaped inside JSON strings,
and every failure silently fell back to ONE term. Fixed 2026-08-30:
line-based TERM: output contract, tolerant parser, corrective retry
(tests/test_search_term_parsing.py). Ten consecutive post-fix calls:
7 terms each. A total-hits threshold would still fail on term-count
variation, so the floor stays per-query.
max_empty is a FRACTION: niche angle-terms crossed with narrow tier
filters legitimately return zeros. The malformed-query signature is
MOST queries empty (25/28 = 89% in the regression), not some.
The harness reads these numbers from a shared audit log with no run
identity, so it skips esearch assertions when >10 terms appear in the
window (impossible from one run = concurrent retrieval interleaved).

baseline.note: Live route, retrieval only, via eval/run_eval.py after the Cochrane journal-scoping fix. Recorded as a RANGE over 4 consecutive runs, not a point: search terms are LLM-generated and the term count is not stable, so a point baseline would read as a regression on the next run. Thresholds are floors, set well below the observed range.
baseline.cochrane_note: 1 genuine Cochrane Database review in every run, down from the falsely-reported 10. This is the stable number and the one to watch.
baseline.variance_note: The 2x spread in paper count tracked term-count flapping (1 vs 3 with parse luck), fixed 2026-08-30 - see post_generator_fix.

post_generator_fix.note: First clean run after the term-generator fix (stable 7-8 terms). Papers roughly tripled vs the 1-term runs; expect future runs near this shape.

full_curriculum_reference.note: The 2026-08-29 17:29 run WITH synthesis, the only end-to-end cost measurement. run_eval.py does retrieval only and costs no LLM tokens.
full_curriculum_reference.cost_note: Four modules with real retrieval. Above the $0.50 target, and this is the honest number to quote. The failing 5-paper run cost $0.5968 - it met the target by not retrieving anything, so cost per run is not a quality metric.

regression_reference.note: The failing run, kept so the diff stays legible.

cases.question: Use of lasers in root canal disinfection
why: Companion to laser-root-canal-disinfection-live. Same question, other
path. The live case guards search-term generation; this one guards what
write-back actually deposited - if the 196 written-back papers were
mistiered or thinly embedded, this case degrades while the live case
stays green.
Pinned to library for the mirror-image reason the other is pinned to
live: without the pin, a library that lost coverage would silently fall
through to PubMed and the case would pass by measuring the wrong path.

baseline.note: Retrieval only, via scripts/probe_retrieval.py, after the Cochrane tier fix and the 109-row demotion.
baseline.cochrane_note: All three are genuine Cochrane Database reviews on adjacent topics, not laser-specific. That is the honest answer for a topic Cochrane has not reviewed.
